key_highlights: ASX ended the week higher driven by banking strength and US Fed rate pause, despite persistent retail weakness.
Strait of Hormuz supertanker mine strike and Middle East stalemate inject fresh upside risk into global crude and energy equities.
Domestic macro pressures intensify as RBA hawkishness hits households, accelerating Sydney and Melbourne property market downturns.
Corporate divergence widens with Coles losing market share to Woolworths, alongside regulatory probes into failed mega-floats.

sectors.trend: Bullish supply shock driven by Hormuz tanker mine strike and Iranian geopolitical stalemate.
sectors.implications: Favourable near-term earnings tailwind for upstream producers (WDS.AX, STO.AX); elevated domestic energy transition and gas policy scrutiny.

sectors.trend: Major banks rally on resilient net interest margins and global rate pause, despite rising mortgage stress.
sectors.implications: Big four banks (CBA.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX, ANZ.AX) anchor index stability, though housing market softness threatens credit growth.

sectors.trend: Severe consumer squeeze due to high RBA cash rates; competitive market share shifts within grocery duopoly.
sectors.implications: Coles (COL.AX) de-rates after heavy valuation loss to Woolworths (WOW.AX); discretionary retail remains vulnerable to spending contraction.

sectors.trend: Iron ore sentiment remains volatile while selective exploration interest supports junior gold and silver miners.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, and FMG.AX track Chinese demand signals; precious metal developers see tactical rotation amid macro uncertainty.

sectors.trend: Rapid housing price declines across Sydney (-10%) and Melbourne alongside multi-year low auction clearance rates.
sectors.implications: Headwinds for residential developers and diversified property trusts (SGP.AX, DXS.AX, MGR.AX) as debt refinancing costs remain elevated.

sectors.trend: Heightened scrutiny following mega-float ASIC probes and global crypto cybersecurity breaches.
sectors.implications: Risk-off stance toward speculative tech; growing local community resistance to AI data centre expansion.

key_themes: Monetary policy divergence: Fed rate pause supporting risk appetite against hawkish RBA stance compressing Australian household budgets.
Geopolitical commodity volatility: Oil supply disruptions countering softened industrial metal sentiment.
Residential property correction: Accelerated price declines in Sydney and Melbourne filtering into bank loan book risks.

risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight defensive, cash-generative equities with low consumer discretionary exposure.
Hedge via long upstream energy positions and domestic gas exposure.
Underweight residential REITs and monitor major bank loan impairment provisions.
Avoid unlisted speculative floats and companies with high unhedged digital asset exposures.

opportunities.rationale: Crude price spikes following Hormuz mine attack and ongoing Iranian tension support strong free cash flow yields.

opportunities.recommendation: Long Woolworths relative to Coles pair trade
opportunities.rationale: Woolworths gains market share and operational stability as Coles faces multi-billion valuation de-rating and operational issues.

opportunities.recommendation: Selective exposure to gold and silver producers
opportunities.rationale: Geopolitical escalation and currency hedging dynamics enhance precious metals demand.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Underweight domestic discretionary retail and residential developers
defensive_moves.rationale: Household cash flows face ongoing compression from high RBA rates and sharp home value erosion.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge ASX 200 exposure via index protection
defensive_moves.rationale: Potential rate-driven consumer defaults and sovereign debt concerns in Victoria create broader equity downside risks.

market_outlook.short_term: Range-bound trading for ^AXJO (1–3 months). Energy strength and stable banking margins balance drag from consumer retail and property headwinds.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive outlook (6–12 months). Eventual RBA policy normalization and infrastructure demand will stabilize equity multiples once housing troughs.
